about.title: Selma Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Selma residents rely on local clinics, urgent care centers, and Fresno-area hospitals for everything from routine checkups to emergency treatment. Most of the time, care goes as expected. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgical step is skipped, or medication is administered incorrectly, the consequences can follow a patient for years. California law treats these cases differently than a typical injury claim — there's a shorter window to act, a required notice period before any lawsuit, and rules about expert review that make early legal guidance especially valuable. If you or a family member were harmed by substandard medical care in Selma, understanding your options sooner rather than later matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can review your medical records, explain whether the facts support a claim, and walk you through next steps at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Guidance Matter in a Selma Malpractice Claim

items.title: The Clock Starts Sooner Than You Think
items.desc: Under MICRA, you generally have one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the original injury, to bring a claim. Waiting to explore your options can quietly close that window.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes Before Any Lawsuit
items.desc: California requires a formal 90-day notice to the provider before a malpractice suit can be filed. Missing or mishandling this step can delay or derail an otherwise valid claim.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because a bad medical outcome alone doesn't prove malpractice, a qualified medical expert typically has to confirm the standard of care was breached. An attorney familiar with this process can help line up that review early.

items.question: Does a bad outcome from surgery or treatment automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, and a poor result by itself isn't proof of negligence. A claim generally requires showing the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care, which is why medical expert review is such a central part of these cases.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Selma?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover the injury, but no more than three years from when it happened, whichever comes first. There are limited exceptions, so it's worth getting a records review sooner rather than later, especially since a 90-day pre-suit notice is also required.

items.question: Are there caps on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California law places a statutory cap on non-economic damages (things like pain and suffering), and that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to that same cap.

items.question: I live in Selma but was treated at a hospital outside Fresno County — does that matter?
items.answer: It can affect where a claim is filed and which records need to be gathered, but it doesn't prevent you from pursuing a claim. An independent attorney connected through LawProactive can sort out venue and jurisdiction details as part of reviewing your case.
